engine.summary: 2D nesting of polygons on sheets and 3D packing of boxes in a container, by constructive fills and metaheuristic searches, with checkers that say whether a layout keeps its problem's rules.

surfaces.name: u-nesting
surfaces.error_shape: Err(Error), whose code() is the code and whose variant holds the fields.

surfaces.name: @iyulab/u-nesting
surfaces.note: Objects in and out, typed in the .d.ts (Request2D, SolveResponse, ...); a refusal is thrown. Bundler and Node targets; no bundler-less browser build.
surfaces.error_shape: A thrown Error whose code property is the code, with the fields as its other properties.

surfaces.name: u-nesting
surfaces.error_shape: Nothing raised: the response dict has success False, the code and a details dict holding the fields.

surfaces.name: UNesting
surfaces.note: C ABI wrapper; versioned with the crate.
surfaces.error_shape: A NestingException whose ErrorCode is the code, Parameter and Index the fields of those names, and Details the rest.

errors.shape: A refusal carries a stable snake_case 'code' and the fields listed for that code; how it arrives depends on the surface (error_shape).

source.catalog: CodeCatalog::of_engine in crates/core/src/api_types.rs, read off one example of every refusal and checker violation; published as codes() in WebAssembly and Python, unesting_codes() over the C ABI and Codes on .NET. What each code means is tabled in npm/README.md, which a test holds equal to the catalog.

operations.summary: Places polygon parts on a rectangular or polygonal sheet (or on as many sheets as they need), by the chosen strategy, and reports the placements, the parts left unplaced, the utilization and why the run stopped.

effects.note: The searches (ga, brkga, sa, gdrr, alns) draw from config.seed when it is given and from fresh entropy when it is not; blf and nfp use no randomness.

determinism.note: The worst case, for a search without config.seed. stop_reason says which limit ended a run.

cases.when: strategy blf or nfp, with time_limit_ms 0 (no time limit)
a search (ga, brkga, sa) given config.seed, with time_limit_ms 0: it ends on its own generation budget
strategy blf or nfp, with a time limit (time_limit_ms above 0)
cases.note: A fill stops before its next piece once the limit runs out, so how many pieces it places depends on machine speed; one that finishes in time gives the layout it gives without a limit.

cases.when: a search given config.seed, with a time limit (time_limit_ms above 0)
cases.note: How far the search gets before the limit depends on machine speed; with the same seed it visits the same candidates in the same order.

output_provenance.note: Whether the layout is a finished construction, the best a search found before a budget or the deadline, or a cancelled run's.

limits: Layout quality has not been compared against best-known solutions of standard instances.
Feasibility of every returned layout is checkable with check_2d, which tests keep at zero violations for each strategy.

performance.complexity: Constructive fills: about O(n^2) no-fit-polygon queries in the part count n; searches: that per evaluated layout, until their budget or the deadline.
